Conversations, accepted runs, steering and stopping, and the live event stream

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This is the model the web console uses. An agent has **sessions** (conversations). You send a message to a session and the daemon accepts it as a **run** that executes in the background; progress arrives on the agent's **event stream**. Unlike the blocking `client.agents.run()`, a run survives a dropped connection, and you can steer or stop it.

| Accessor | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `client.sessions` | List, create, read, rename, archive, delete, compact, export and search conversations |
| `client.runs` | Start a run in a session, read it, stop it, list a session's runs |
| `client.events` | The agent's live SSE stream |
| `client.attachments` | Upload and download session files |

<Aside type="caution">
  Every route here is an owner route. A script has to send `Authorization: Bearer <ANIMA_LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN>`; see [Authentication](/sdk/client/#authentication).
</Aside>

## Sessions

```typescript
const main = await client.sessions.main(agentId); // the durable main web conversation
const chat = await client.sessions.create(agentId, { title: 'Release planning' });

const page = await client.sessions.list(agentId, { limit: 20, includeHelpers: false });
for (const session of page.sessions) {
  console.log(session.id, session.title, session.kind, session.activeRuns, session.unread);
}
// page.nextCursor is the cursor for the next page, or null
```

| Method | Returns | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `main(agentId)` | `Session` | Resolves the agent's main web conversation (a `POST`; it creates or adopts one if needed) |
| `list(agentId, options?)` | `SessionPage` | `kind`, `archived`, `q`, `cursor`, `limit` (1 to 200, default 50), `includeHelpers` (default `true`). Newest activity first |
| `get(agentId, sessionId)` | `Session` | A single read also carries `usage` and `contextUsage` |
| `create(agentId, { title? })` | `Session` | Rejected with `429` beyond 60 per minute per agent |
| `update(agentId, sessionId, patch)` | `Session` | `title`, `archived`, `lastReadAtMs` |
| `remove(agentId, sessionId)` | `void` | `409` while a run in it is active; memories are kept |
| `messages(agentId, sessionId, options?)` | `SessionMessagePage` | `before`, `anchor`, `limit`, `includeHidden`; messages oldest to newest, plus `nextBefore` |
| `searchMessages(agentId, { q, limit? })` | `SessionMessageSearchPage` | `{ results, hasMore }` of matching messages across sessions |
| `exportMarkdown(agentId, sessionId)` | `string` | Full transcript as Markdown |
| `compact(agentId, sessionId)` | `Session` | Starts compaction; the summary arrives later as `session.updated` |

`Session.kind` is `chat`, `telegram`, `discord`, `checkin`, `job` or `helper`. Each session also reports `capabilities` (which of `send`, `steer`, `stop`, `rename`, `archive`, `delete`, `compact` and `export` apply to its kind), `messageCount`, `preview`, `pendingApprovals`, an optional `summary` and, when older turns were dropped from model context, `contextTrimmed`. `list()` and `main()` throw `DaemonTooOldError` when the daemon predates sessions.

Session history is complete in the daemon's history store; the `messages` and `messageCount` on an `AgentSnapshot` cover only recent messages.

## Start a Run

```typescript
const { run } = await client.runs.start(
  agentId,
  chat.id,
  { text: 'Draft the release notes for v1.2' },
  { idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() },
);

console.log(run.id, run.status); // usually 'queued'
```

`start(agentId, sessionId, input, { idempotencyKey, signal? })` returns `{ run, steer? }` as soon as the message is accepted.

| `StartRunInput` field | Description |
|-----------------------|-------------|
| `text` | Message text (up to 32 KiB); may be empty only with attachments |
| `attachmentIds` | Up to 10 ids from `client.attachments.upload()` |
| `skill` | Slug of an enabled, active [skill](/sdk/extensions/#skills) whose instructions join this run |
| `mode` | `queue` (default) or `steer` (below) |
| `browserSelection` | Explicit owner opt-in for scoped browser work |
| `timeZone` | The sender's IANA time zone, kept as the owner's |

The `idempotencyKey` is required (1 to 128 visible ASCII characters). Sending the same key again within 24 hours returns the original run and creates nothing; reusing it for a different message is a `409`. Keep one key per logical message and reuse it when you retry.

A queued run waits behind the session's earlier messages. A companion holds at most eight waiting messages; beyond that the daemon answers `429`.

## Follow a Run

### Poll

```typescript
import { isTerminalRunStatus } from '@animaOS-SWARM/sdk';

let current = run;
while (!isTerminalRunStatus(current.status)) {
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
  current = await client.runs.get(agentId, run.id);
}

if (current.status === 'completed' && current.replyMessageId) {
  const { messages } = await client.sessions.messages(agentId, chat.id, { limit: 10 });
  console.log(messages.find((message) => message.id === current.replyMessageId)?.text);
}
```

`RunStatus` is `queued`, `running`, `awaiting_approval`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `interrupted`; the last four are terminal. A run in `awaiting_approval` is waiting for an [approval](/sdk/approvals/) and is not terminal, so a poller should surface it.

### Stream

```typescript
import { isRunLifecycleEvent, isTerminalRunStatus } from '@animaOS-SWARM/sdk';

const controller = new AbortController();

for await (const event of client.events.stream(agentId, { signal: controller.signal })) {
  if (event.type === 'step.delta' && event.runId === run.id) {
    process.stdout.write(event.text);
  }
  if (isRunLifecycleEvent(event) && event.run.id === run.id && isTerminalRunStatus(event.run.status)) {
    break;
  }
}
```

`client.events.stream(agentId, { signal? })` yields typed `AgentEvent` objects for the agent, its helpers and sessions delegated from it. Behavior to design around:

- The first event is `stream.snapshot`: the active runs with their current step text (up to 64 KiB) and tool cards, plus pending approvals.
- There is no replay. A reconnect starts from a fresh snapshot, and `Last-Event-ID` is ignored.
- A consumer that falls behind receives `stream.resync` (with `missed`) and keeps going; refetch state when you see it.
- Each agent allows 16 open streams; more are refused with `429`.

| Event `type` | Meaning |
|--------------|---------|
| `stream.snapshot`, `stream.resync` | Stream start state; missed events |
| `session.created`, `session.updated`, `session.deleted` | Session changes |
| `run.queued`, `run.started`, `run.awaiting_approval`, `run.completed`, `run.failed`, `run.cancelled`, `run.interrupted` | Run lifecycle (carry the `run`) |
| `run.progress` | A phase such as `compacting` |
| `run.steered` | A steering message was read by the run |
| `step.delta` | Streamed text (`stepId`, `offset`, `text`) |
| `message.created` | A message was saved (`messageId`, `role`) |
| `tool.started`, `tool.finished` | Tool activity with bounded previews |
| `model.fallback` | A fallback model answered instead of the primary |
| `approval.requested`, `approval.resolved` | Approval changes (carry the `approval`) |
| `skill.updated`, `automation.updated` | Skills or automations changed; read them again |

Helpers `isRunLifecycleEvent`, `isApprovalEvent`, `isSkillEvent` and `isAutomationEvent` narrow the union. Every event has `agentId`, optional `sessionId` and `runId`, a per-stream `seq` and a timestamp `at`.

## Steer and Stop

```typescript
// Join the session's active run before its next model call
const steered = await client.runs.start(
  agentId,
  chat.id,
  { text: 'Also cover the migration notes', mode: 'steer' },
  { idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() },
);
console.log(steered.steer?.status); // 'pending' when it joined a running run

// Stop a run
const stopped = await client.runs.stop(agentId, run.id);
```

`mode: 'steer'` joins the running run and returns that run with `steer: { status: 'pending' }`. With no active run to join, the message is queued like any other. A steer the run never reads becomes a queued message after the run ends.

`runs.stop()` cancels a queued run at once, and ends a running one at its next checkpoint. Stopping again, or stopping a finished run, changes nothing. Tools already running finish, except that a `bash` command is killed; background processes keep running, and completed effects are not undone.

## Runs

```typescript
const recent = await client.runs.listForSession(agentId, chat.id, { limit: 10 }); // newest first
```

A `Run` has `id`, `agentId`, `sessionId`, `source` (`web`, `api`, `telegram`, `discord`, `schedule`, `job`, `delegation` or `peer`), `status`, `input`, timestamps, `error`, `usage`, `model`, `provider`, `steps`, `parentRunId`, `replyMessageId` and, when recorded, `actionReceipts`. Action receipts are bounded records of each tool call (`started`, `succeeded` or `failed`); `started` means the outcome is unknown, so inspect effects before retrying work after an interruption.

## Attachments

```typescript
const { attachment } = await client.attachments.upload(agentId, chat.id, file, 'notes.txt');
await client.runs.start(
  agentId,
  chat.id,
  { text: 'Summarize this', attachmentIds: [attachment.id] },
  { idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() },
);

const bytes = await client.attachments.download(agentId, attachment.id);
```

Uploads are saved in the agent's configured workspace, so configure a workspace first. Limits include 10 MiB per image, 1 MiB per text file and 25 MiB per PDF or Office document. See [Workspace & Capabilities](/sdk/workspace/).

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The animaOS terminal UI is built with [Ink](https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink) and runs in your terminal. It is a client of the Rust daemon: `animaos launch` creates a swarm from your `anima.yaml` on the daemon, subscribes to its event stream, and draws the agents, messages, tool calls and results as they arrive. It is not the main surface for everyday use of anima (that is the web console); it is a lightweight way to run and watch an agent team from a workspace.

<Aside type="caution">
  The TUI sits behind `animaos launch`. `animaos run` and `animaos chat` are plain text and never render it, and `animaos launch --no-tui` is the plain-text mode.
</Aside>

## In This Section

- [Commands & States](/tui/commands/) covers slash commands, keys and daemon-down behavior.
- [History & Resume](/tui/history/) covers saved runs, `anima-history.json`, `/resume`, `/retry` and undoing deletes.

## Recommended Flow

1. Start the daemon.

   ```bash
   bun run daemon
   ```

2. Create a workspace, or write an `anima.yaml` by hand for a team.

   ```bash
   animaos create agent content-writer -d "Research topics and write articles"
   ```

3. Launch it in the TUI.

   ```bash
   cd content-writer
   animaos launch
   ```

## Launch Modes

```bash
animaos launch                       # interactive TUI session
animaos launch "Build a website"     # one task in the TUI, then exit
animaos launch --no-tui "Build a website"   # plain text, for scripts and CI
```

- **Interactive** (no task) opens an input bar. Each task you enter runs on the swarm, and past runs stay available. If the workspace has saved history, the last run opens first as a resumed result.
- **One task** runs it, shows the live view, and exits when you press Enter, Esc or `q`. While it is on screen, `t` opens the trace, `h` the history and `r` reruns the task.

`launch` seeds daemon memories from `agents/<slug>/memory/seed.json`, saves run history in the workspace, and in the TUI writes the latest task and result to `anima-result.md`.

## What You See

The live swarm view stacks these panels:

| Panel | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Header** | Strategy, agent count (and how many are active) and the current task |
| **Agents** | The configured agents plus any live ones, with status (`idle`, `thinking`, `running_tool`, `done`, `error`) and tokens |
| **Messages** | The latest agent-to-agent and lifecycle messages |
| **Tools** | The latest tool calls with status, truncated arguments and duration |
| **Past runs** | In interactive mode, the three most recent saved runs |
| **Status bar** | Total tokens, elapsed seconds, agent count, `gaps` when events were missed, and `daemon: up` or `daemon: down` with the last check time |
| **Input bar** | In interactive mode, where you type tasks and slash commands |

Other full-screen views open from commands: the saved-run **History** and **Resume** browser, the **Trace** of messages and tool activity, a single **Result**, and the **Agents** editor.

## Operator States

- **Preflight check.** `launch` checks `GET /health` before the TUI starts and shows a warning if the daemon is unreachable.
- **Health polling.** While the TUI is open it rechecks the daemon about every 5 seconds.
- **Command-only mode.** When the daemon is down, the input bar blocks tasks (`daemon down - tasks paused; use /health or /help`) but still accepts commands such as `/health`, `/help`, `/history` and `/trace`.
- **Recovery.** When the daemon returns, a recovery notice appears and tasks work again.
- **Gaps.** If the daemon reports that your event stream fell behind (`swarm:lagged`), the status bar shows a `gaps` count so you know the trace has holes.

## Live Telemetry

The TUI subscribes to the swarm's SSE stream: task starts and completions, tool calls with arguments and results, per-agent token usage, and the final result. The same stream is available to your own code through the [SDK](/sdk/swarms/events/).

## Editing Agents

`/agents` opens the agent profiles from `anima.yaml`. Select an agent to view its profile; press `e` to edit `bio`, `lore`, `adjectives`, `topics`, `knowledge`, `style` and `system`, and Ctrl+S to save. Saving writes `anima.yaml` and makes the next task build a fresh swarm. Because `anima.yaml` is rewritten from the fields `launch` reads, fields it ignores (such as `mission` and `values`) are dropped on save.

<Aside type="tip">
  The TUI works best in a terminal with true color and at least 80 columns by 24 rows. Set `NO_COLOR` to turn colors off.
</Aside>

## Slash Commands

In the swarm view:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/agents` | Browse and edit the agent profiles from `anima.yaml` |
| `/history` | Browse past runs |
| `/resume [label]` | Browse saved runs, or open one by label (prefix and partial matches work; it suggests close ones) |
| `/rename <label>` | Name the current (or most recent) saved run |
| `/delete <label>` | Delete a saved run by exact label; repeat the command to confirm |
| `/undo` | Restore the last deleted saved run |
| `/undo-drop` | Discard the oldest queued undo; repeat to confirm |
| `/undo-status` | Show the deleted-run undo queue |
| `/trace` | Inspect the messages and tool activity of the last run |
| `/result` | Open the full last result |
| `/status` | Show session state: phase, task, agents, daemon, message and tool counts, history size |
| `/health` | Recheck daemon connectivity and report healthy, recovered or unavailable |
| `/retry` | Rerun the last task (hidden while the daemon is down) |
| `/help` | List the commands available right now |
| `/clear` | Clear the session and delete the saved history file |
| `/exit` (or `/quit`) | Leave the TUI |

In a result view, `/back` returns to the swarm view, and `/delete` and `/rename` act on the open run. While the daemon is down, a result view offers `/health` and `/help` instead of `/retry`. An unknown command shows `Unknown command: /name. Type /help for commands.`

Saved-run labels are a name you give with `/rename`. `/resume`, `/rename` and `/delete` complete labels with Tab.

## Keys

| Key | Where | Action |
|-----|-------|--------|
| `Enter` | Input bar | Submit the task or command (or pick the highlighted command) |
| `Tab` | Input bar | Complete the highlighted slash command or saved-run label |
| `↑` / `↓` | Input bar | Move through command suggestions; otherwise recall earlier inputs (up to 100) |
| `Ctrl+R` | Input bar | Search earlier inputs; press again for the next match, Esc to restore your draft |
| `Ctrl+O` | Swarm view, between tasks | Open saved runs to resume |
| `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+P`, `Ctrl+Y` | After a `/resume` with several matches | Move through the matches and open the selected one |
| `s` | While a task is running | Show status |
| `Ctrl+C` | Anywhere | Quit |

Browsers inside the TUI (History, Trace, Agents) share a few keys: `↑` and `↓` to move, `/` to search, `n` and `N` for the next and previous match, `Esc` to clear a search, and `q` (or `Esc`) to go back.

## Operator States

### Healthy daemon

Task submission is enabled. The TUI streams events, tool traces, token updates and final results as they arrive.

### Daemon unavailable

When a health check fails (at launch, or about every 5 seconds while the TUI is open):

- a warning appears above the panels, and the status bar shows `daemon: down`
- the input bar reads `daemon down - tasks paused; use /health or /help`, and plain tasks are refused
- `/health` and `/help` still work, as do the browsing commands (`/history`, `/trace`, `/result`, `/agents`)

### Recovery

When the daemon answers again, the TUI shows a recovery message and re-enables tasks. `/health` forces a recheck at any time.

### Missed events

If the daemon reports that the TUI's stream fell behind, the status bar shows a `gaps` count. Rerun the task if you need a complete trace.

<Aside type="tip">
  For one plain-text answer, use `animaos run`. Use `animaos launch` for a session with history, retry, live telemetry and recovery.
</Aside>

`animaos launch` keeps a local record of the tasks it runs, so you can reopen a result, rerun a task or give a run a name after the session ends.

## Where History Lives

For a workspace launched with `animaos launch`, history is stored in `anima-history.json` next to `anima.yaml`. The newest 100 entries are kept. Each entry records the task, its result text, whether it failed, a timestamp and an optional label. Both TUI and `--no-tui` launches append to it.

When an interactive session starts and the file has entries, the TUI opens the most recent one as a resumed result.

<Aside type="note">
  History is local CLI state, not a daemon API. Conversation history on the daemon (sessions and messages) is separate; see [Sessions & Runs](/sdk/sessions/).
</Aside>

## Browsing

- `/history` opens the run browser with the newest run selected.
- `/resume` opens the browser for resuming: named runs first, then the rest newest first, with the first one selected.
- `/resume <label>` opens a run directly. Matching tries an exact label, then a prefix, then a substring. With several matches, the TUI shows up to three and you pick with Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+Y; with none, it suggests the closest labels.
- Ctrl+O opens saved runs between tasks.

In the browser: `↑` and `↓` move, `/` searches task and result text (`n` and `N` jump between matches), Enter opens the selected run, `r` retries it, and `q`, `b` or Esc returns.

## Resumed Views

Opening a run shows its task and result. From there:

- `/back` returns to the swarm view.
- `/retry` reruns the task when the daemon is healthy. While the daemon is down it is unavailable, and `/health` rechecks.
- `/rename <label>` names the run so you can find it again with `/resume`.
- `/delete` removes it.

## Naming, Deleting and Undoing

Names are labels you set with `/rename`; a label already used by another run is refused, and the TUI suggests the next free one. In the resume browser, `x` deletes the selected run (press it again to confirm). From the input bar, `/delete <label>` needs an exact label and asks you to repeat the command; any other command cancels the pending delete.

Deleted runs go into an undo queue of up to five. `/undo` (or `u` in the resume browser) restores the most recent one, `/undo-status` shows the queue, and `/undo-drop` (or `D`, pressed twice) discards the oldest queued entry. The queue lives in memory for the session. After a delete or a rename the history file is rewritten.

`/clear` empties the session, the undo queue and the history file.

## Retrying

`/retry` reruns the open run's task, or the last task if none is open. A retry is a new run, so it adds a new entry rather than overwriting the old one.

## Suggested Workflow

1. Launch a workspace with `animaos launch`.
2. Run a few tasks.
3. Use `/history` to inspect earlier runs, and `/rename` to name the ones worth keeping.
4. Next session, use `/resume <label>` and `/retry` to continue.
